name: Thiamine-Responsive Maple Syrup Urine Disease

criteria.description: Elevated plasma levels of branched-chain amino acids (leucine, isoleucine, valine)
Clinical and biochemical improvement upon thiamine supplementation
Deficiency or dysfunction of branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex confirmed by enzymatic assay or genetic testing
Characteristic sweet maple syrup odor in urine
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with thiamine-responsive MSUD (e.g., DBT gene mutations)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Elevated branched-chain amino acids plus clinical response to thiamine supplementation and confirmation of BCKD complex deficiency
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is supported by biochemical, enzymatic, and genetic testing along with clinical response to thiamine.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sweet maple syrup odor in urine
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic odor due to accumulation of branched-chain keto acids

searchTerms: high levels of certain amino acids in blood

pathognomonic.notes: Includes lethargy, irritability, and developmental delay

common.notes: Impaired coordination due to central nervous system involvement
Common in infants during metabolic crises
Reduced muscle tone observed in affected infants
Delayed acquisition of motor and cognitive milestones

occasional.notes: Increased muscle tone in some cases
Enlarged liver observed in some patients

rare.notes: Peripheral nerve dysfunction in some cases

laboratory: Elevated plasma branched-chain amino acids (leucine, isoleucine, valine)
Elevated branched-chain keto acids in urine
imaging: MRI brain showing cerebral edema or demyelination during crises
other: Positive clinical response to high-dose thiamine supplementation
Enzymatic assay showing partial BCKD complex activity

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of response to thiamine supplementation
Distinct odor of sweaty feet instead of maple syrup

redFlags: Rapid neurological deterioration during metabolic crises
references: Chuang DT, Shih VE. Maple syrup urine disease (branched-chain ketoaciduria). In: Scriver CR, et al., editors. The Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease. 8th ed. McGraw-Hill; 2001.
